extracted.intended_audience: attorneys practicing before the United States Patent and Trademark Office (especially those who are or were USPTO employees) and USPTO disciplinary officers
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order of discipline addressing an attorney-respondent's violations of federal ethics statutes and USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, and prescribing sanctions, notice, reinstatement, and compliance requirements. Relevant to adjudicating or complying with USPTO attorney-discipline matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on receiving compensation for representational services (18 U.S.C. §203)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 18 U.S.C. § 203, federal employees (other than for the proper discharge of his or her official duties) are prohibited, inter alia, from directly or indirectly receiving or agreeing to receive compensation for any representational services as an attorney, rendered either personally or by another, at a time when such person is an employee of the United States or agency of the United States in relation to any application, proceeding, or other particular matter in which the United States is a party or has a direct and substantial interest before any department or agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative application: preparing, filing, or prosecuting trademark applications or acting as attorney of record before the USPTO while employed by the USPTO can trigger this prohibition even if no payment was actually received. Employee must avoid agreeing to compensated representation in covered matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on acting as attorney before agencies in covered matters (18 U.S.C. §205)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 18 U.S.C. § 205, federal employees are prohibited (other than for the proper discharge of his or her federal employment duties) from, inter alia, acting as an attorney for anyone before any agency in connection with any covered matter in which the United States is a party or has a direct and substantial interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies regardless of compensation; representing others before an agency in 'covered matters' while employed by the government is barred unless undertaken as part of official duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice before the Office by Government employees subject to conflict-of-interest laws (37 C.F.R. §11.10(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 11.10(e) provides that '[p]ractice before the Office by Government employees is subject to any applicable conflict of interest laws, regulations or codes of professional responsibility.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government-employee practitioners must comply with applicable conflict-of-interest statutes/regulations and seek guidance when uncertain; the OED notified the respondent of this rule in an investigative letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engaging in conduct contrary to applicable federal ethics law (37 C.F.R. §11.111)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 11.111 — engaging in conduct contrary to applicable federal ethics law while a Federal Government employee including conflict of interest statutes and regulations of the department, agency, or commission — was found violated by 'preparing, filing, and prosecuting trademark applications before the Office and filing a substantive motion with the TTAB on behalf of a third party while an employee of the Office; and, not withdrawing as attorney of record in numerous trademark matters pending before the Office upon being notified of the prohibition on practicing before the Office while an employee.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule defines misconduct when government-employees engage in outside practice that conflicts with federal ethics obligations and fail to cease representation upon notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practicing law in violation of jurisdictional regulations (37 C.F.R. §11.505)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 11.505 — practicing law in a jurisdiction in violation of the regulation of the legal profession — was found violated by preparing, filing, and prosecuting trademark applications before the Office and filing a substantive motion with the TTAB on behalf of a third party while an employee of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A USPTO practitioner must not undertake legal practice before the Office if such practice contravenes applicable jurisdictional or professional regulations governing the practice of law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice (37 C.F.R. §11.804(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d) — engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice — was found by reference to the respondent's preparing, filing, and prosecuting trademark applications and filing a substantive TTAB motion on behalf of a third party while an employee and failing to withdraw upon notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard encompasses actions by practitioners that undermine fair administration of proceedings, including failure to adhere to ethical prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to withdraw when representation will result in violation (37 C.F.R. §11.116(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 11.116(a)(1) — representing a client, or where representation has commenced, failing to withdraw from the representation of a client if the representation will result in violation of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct or other law — was found violated by not withdrawing from representing others in numerous trademark matters pending before the Office while employed by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must withdraw when continued representation would violate USPTO rules or other law; failure to do so is actionable misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Director/OED jurisdiction over disciplinary matters (35 U.S.C. §§2(b)(2)(D) and 32; 37 C.F.R. §§11.19, 11.20, 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26. Respondent is subject to disciplinary jurisdiction as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.19 pertaining to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101–11.901).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory and regulatory provisions provide the Office authority to investigate, charge, resolve, and sanction practitioners for violations of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: suspension from practice before the Office in trademark and other non-patent matters (30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the Office in trademark and other non-patent matters for thirty (30) days commencing on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension bars practice in listed matters for the stated period; reinstatement eligibility and other conditions (see reinstatement and prohibitions) apply. Suspension remains in effect until the OED Director grants reinstatement per §11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and petition requirements for reinstatement (37 C.F.R. §11.60(c); 37 C.F.R. §1.21(a)(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: After serving 30 days of suspension, the respondent may file a petition for reinstatement with the OED Director pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(c), accompanied by the fee required by 37 C.F.R. § 1.21(a)(10). The petition shall contain a statement attesting to compliance with the Final Order including a sworn declaration that she has not engaged in the practice of trademark or other non-patent law before the Office during the period of suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is not automatic; petition must comply with procedural and evidentiary requirements and the OED Director retains rights under §11.60(e) and (f) to act on petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions on practice, advertising, holding out, and rendering services while suspended or employed (37 C.F.R. §11.58(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not hold herself out as authorized to practice law before the Office pursuant to § 11.58(b)(3); shall not advertise availability or ability to perform legal services for any person having immediate or prospective business before the Office pursuant to § 11.58(b)(4); shall not render legal advice or services to any person having immediate or prospective business before the Office as to that business pursuant to § 11.58(b)(5); respondent is not granted limited recognition under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(c). These prohibitions apply unless and until she is reinstated and is no longer an employee of the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During suspension and while employed by USPTO, the practitioner must cease all relevant practice-related communications and services involving the Office. Limited recognition (practice under limited authorization) is expressly denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification obligations to jurisdictions and clients (37 C.F.R. §11.58(b)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall provide notice, by certified mail, return receipt requested, of the Final Order to all State and Federal jurisdictions and administrative agencies in which the Respondent is admitted to practice within 30 days of entry of the Final Order, and shall inform by certified mail all clients who have immediate or prospective business before the Office of her inability to act on their behalf after the start of her suspension, the need to consult with other counsel, and of any immediate deadlines; except a client who, before the start of suspension, has consented to another registered practitioner taking over the representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must be timely and by certified mail; includes a client-notice exception for prior consent to substitution of counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirement for compliance steps (37 C.F.R. §11.58(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall keep and maintain records of the various steps taken pursuant to the Final Order, pursuant to § 11.58(d), so that in any subsequent proceeding proof of compliance with the Final Order will be available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain documentary proof of notices sent, withdrawals, and other compliance actions to demonstrate adherence if later reviewed or used in future proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice by the Office; waiver of publication requirement (37 C.F.R. §11.60(g); §11.3(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided Notice of Suspension language. The publication requirement set forth in § 11.60(g) is waived pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.3(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will make discipline public via its reading room and the Official Gazette; the Final Order specifies the content of the Official Gazette notice. Certain publication formalities were waived in this settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order shall prevent the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including this Final Order: (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct concerning Respondent; (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding against Respondent (i) as an aggravating factor to be taken into consideration in determining any discipline to be imposed, and/or (ii) to rebut any representation by or on Respondent's behalf; and (3) in connection with any request for reinstatement submitted by Respondent pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner should expect that this record may be used against them in future complaints, proceedings, or reinstatement determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to seek guidance and prior ethics training notice (employee responsibilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent signed a 'Statement Relating to Employee Responsibilities and Conduct' acknowledging responsibility to seek guidance on conflict of interest laws and other aspects of employee responsibilities (5 C.F.R. § 2635). Respondent also attended DOC ethics training informing attendees they may not engage in prohibited activities such as the practice of law or working for someone who has matters pending before their office, and the prohibition on contacting the government on behalf of another person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees are obligated to seek ethics guidance and are typically trained that practice before their employing agency is restricted; failure to seek guidance after notice can be an aggravating factor.
